- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (sentiment > 0.7) — model tends to overshoot, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to capture downward momentum or mean reversion.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes — forecast lags behind true price after a spike, often by 1–3 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model exhibits lagging behavior — forecasts don’t adjust quickly enough to sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after strong upward moves, failing to reflect long-term equilibrium.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early cycles (e.g., 2025-09) — true outcomes show stronger downward correction than model suggests.
- Sentiment-driven correction: if sentiment is high and price rises, model should reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overcorrection.
